item.title: Instagram adds AI creative assistant to standalone Edits app
item.description:
Instagram adds AI creative assistant to standalone Edits app

Instagram has announced a new AI-powered “creative assistant” within its standalone Edits app designed to provide creators with feedback and suggestions for their posts.

🧩 How it works

The AI creative assistant analyzes data and metrics from a user’s Instagram account, including:

  • Likes
  • Views
  • Shares
  • Retention on videos

Instagram states that the tool can identify patterns over time to provide suggestions that exceed what metrics alone can offer.

⚙️ Key details

Creators can use the assistant to ask open-ended questions and receive guidance on several areas:

Category AI Assistance Capabilities
Content Analysis Why one video worked and another didn’t, and which content resonated most
Trend Tracking What is trending on Instagram and which audio tracks are trending
Creative Guidance Ideas for content, how to hook viewers, caption suggestions, and video scripting

🚀 Availability

The new feature is free for creators to use up to a certain point. Meta says “power users” have the option to purchase a Meta One subscription for increased usage.

💡 Why it matters

This development follows similar moves by YouTube, which recently updated its AI-powered dashboard (initially announced in 2025) to include A/B testing and AI editing to help creators maximize engagement. While both platforms now offer personalized advice on how to navigate the algorithm, tools like CrowdTangle—previously used by journalists and researchers to monitor popular content on Meta platforms—have been restricted or shut down.

#Instagram #Meta #AI #ContentCreation #SocialMedia

Source: Instagram is adding an AI ‘assistant’ to tell you how to post

item.title: Meta's Instagram AI Labeling System Erroneously Tags Original and Minorly Edited Photos
item.description:
Meta’s Instagram AI Labeling System Erroneously Tags Original and Minorly Edited Photos

Instagram’s system for labeling synthetically generated content has recently gone haywire. Over the last few weeks, users have reported that Meta is automatically applying an “AI Content” label to original photos that were not created or edited with generative AI, while failing to tag actual AI images that should be labeled.

🔍 Overview

Users are reporting widespread issues with Instagram’s automatic labeling system. The visible AI labels, which are intended to help people quickly identify synthetic content at a glance, are instead being placed on original photography. This includes images with minor touch-ups, such as negligible blemish-fixing or edits made with basic design tools.

⚙️ Key Details

Several specific issues and edge cases have emerged regarding the erroneous tags:

  • Canva Integration: Content strategist Jess Bruno flagged concerns regarding Canva’s Background Remover tool. Canva explained that some of its assistive AI tools “were being tagged as generative.” While Canva claims the issue is now resolved on its end, some Threads users report that using the tool still results in their images being tagged. Conversely, other users report that none of their images edited prior to the fix were tagged, and the tool did not apply the C2PA metadata that Meta uses for detection.
  • Poisoned Content: One user discovered that Meta applied the AI tag to an image that had been “poisoned”—subtly tweaked to make it useless for AI training or to degrade AI models—while leaving an unpoisoned version of the same content untagged.
  • Brand Accounts: The cosmetics company About Face, founded by the singer Halsey, had the “AI Content” tag automatically applied to its recent Instagram photos. The brand’s social manager clarified to commenters that no AI was used to create the images.
  • Metadata Misalignment: Certain Apple Intelligence tools in iOS 27 (Spatial Reframing, Extend, and Clean Up) embed Google’s invisible SynthID watermark. Although tagged images in these recent mishaps do not have SynthID embedded, the Meta label claims it detected signals that typically identify content as “entirely AI-generated” rather than merely modified.

🧩 How it works

In February, Meta announced it would scan images for IPTC and C2PA metadata to determine with reasonable certainty whether generative AI was used to create or edit them.

In 2024, this detection system swept up pictures whose Adobe metadata indicated minor generative AI retouching, even if the final photograph was substantively unchanged. While Meta promised to tweak its approach to better reflect the amount of AI used, the latest erroneous labels do not have a clear link to generative AI usage. Outside of these mishaps, testing indicates that the label was only applied on images edited or fully generated using the Meta AI app.

#Instagram #Meta #AILabeling #GenerativeAI

Source: Instagram’s AI detection is a mess (again)

item.title: Instagram to Limit Reach of Unlabeled AI-Generated Profiles
item.description:
Instagram to Limit Reach of Unlabeled AI-Generated Profiles

Instagram is implementing new measures to address the rise of fake AI-influencer accounts that have become increasingly difficult to detect.

⚙️ Key details

Instagram is introducing the following changes to identify AI-generated personas:

  • Label Update: The “AI creator” label is being renamed to “AI-generated profile” to clarify when a profile features an AI-generated person rather than a real human being.
  • Enforcement: The platform will identify accounts that fail to self-label their AI-generated profiles.
  • Penalties: Accounts that do not self-label will have their reach limited, meaning their posts will not be recommended to non-followers in Explore and Reels.
  • Appeals: Profile owners have the option to appeal if they are wrongly flagged.

💡 Why it matters

Instagram stated in a blog post, “We’ve heard that people don’t like seeing a profile that seems human, only to find out later that the person featured is AI-generated,” adding that users “want to know when a profile features an AI-generated person.”

🧩 How it works

User Type Label Requirement
AI-generated person Must self-label as an “AI-generated profile”
People using AI tools for content No label required

#Instagram #AI #SocialMedia #AIInfluencers

Source: Instagram cracks down on AI accounts pretending to be human
